transcript.content: Hello, welcome to the clinic. What brings you in to see us today?

I'm here because I really need some help dealing with a group of people who are constantly monitoring me. I know they are watching my apartment and tracking where I go, and it's getting very hard to handle. I'm hoping you can help me figure out how to make them stop.
Have you been experiencing any unusual mood swings, feelings of depression, or episodes of excessively elevated mood or energy?
No, I haven't really noticed anything like that. My mood has been pretty stable and normal, other than just feeling stressed about being watched.
Have you experienced any voices or sounds that other people can't hear, or seen things that aren't really there, in addition to feeling like you're being watched?
No, I don't hear voices or see things that aren't there. It's not like that at all—I just know for a fact that they are physically watching my apartment and tracking my movements.
How long have you believed that you're being watched and monitored by this group of people?
This has been going on for about five months now. It started back in the spring, and it hasn't stopped since then.

It sounds incredibly stressful to feel like you are constantly being watched, and I can hear how much of a toll this worry is taking on you. While we are in this clinical space together, I want to assure you that you are safe here, and my main focus is helping you find ways to manage this intense stress. Have you been able to discuss these feelings with a close friend, family member, or a healthcare professional who can support you right now?
Have you been able to discuss these feelings with a close friend, family member, or someone you trust about being watched, and how have they responded to your concerns?
I haven't really discussed this with anyone else yet. I've kept it to myself because I'm not sure how they would react or if they would even believe me.
Has this belief that you're being watched affected your daily life, such as your ability to work, maintain relationships, or perform routine tasks?

For the most part, I'm still able to go to work every day, do my chores, and manage my routine without any major issues. I have to be a lot more cautious and alert when I'm out, which is exhausting, but it hasn't stopped me from getting things done. Apart from the constant stress of being watched, my daily life is pretty normal.
I'm sorry, I didn't catch that last part. Could you please repeat your question?
Can you tell me more about what specifically makes you think that this group of people is watching you, and what evidence you have to support this belief?

I don't have physical proof to show you, but it's a very strong, constant feeling that I am being observed. Whenever I'm at home or walking outside, I just feel this intense anxiety that someone is tracking my movements. It's a deeply unsettling feeling that I can't seem to shake off.
Do you think this belief that you're being watched could possibly be a mistaken idea or misinterpretation of things that are actually harmless, or are you completely convinced that it's real?

It's definitely not a mistake, and it is honestly frustrating that you'd suggest I'm just misinterpreting things. The signs are far too obvious to be a coincidence, and I am completely convinced that this is actually happening. There is simply no way I am imagining this.
